description:
FILED s473t6b (Opus, 2026-09-17) by #1501 round 9.

PERL: `%SIG` is a MAGIC hash (Perl_magic_setsig / magic_getsig).  Storing a
STRING handler name qualifies it with the current package, so reading it back
gives the qualified name; deleting it answers that same qualified name and
then the key reads undef.

PCL: `%SIG` is an ordinary hash (`(defvar %SIG ...)` in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp),
so the string is stored and returned verbatim.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL), the shape of t/op/magic.t:671-678:

    $SIG{INT} = "int";
    printf "get=[%s]\n", $SIG{INT};
    printf "del=[%s]\n", delete $SIG{INT};

    perl: get=[main::int]  del=[main::int]
    PCL:  get=[int]        del=[int]

ROWS: baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv op/magic.t 135 `Can assign to __WARN__`,
136 `Can delete from __WARN__`, 139 `Can assign to INT`, 140 `Can delete from
INT`.  (The file's `$SIG{HUNGRY}` rows -- a name that is not a signal -- pass,
because perl does not qualify those either... measured: it DOES store the
string verbatim for a non-signal key, which is why only the four rows above
fail.)

SHAPE: this is a MAGIC HASH, which PCL does not have for `%SIG` -- the store
has no hook.  The cheap honest version is a magic cell on the hash itself (the
`%ENV` sibling, if that one is magic; check before designing), or the store
site if codegen can be made to route `$SIG{...} = ...` through a setter.  Do
NOT special-case the four names: the rule is "a string handler is qualified
with the package in force at the STORE", which is a property of the hash.

Four rows -- a filler.  Note the two `*extra*` rows the same file reports
(`Push a constant on a magic array`, `Assign a constant to a magic hash`) are
NOT this: they are alignment artifacts of the file's own renumbering.


=== HALF DONE (s494g, 2026-09-25, Opus) -- the SIGNAL-key half ===
#2107's %SIG store seam (%p-sig-qualify in %p-sig-set) now qualifies a bare handler NAME with `main::` for every SIGNAL key (always main, probed 5.40.3, even under `package P`); IGNORE / DEFAULT / "" / a name with `::` or `'` are stored as given.  magic.t `Can assign to INT` / `Can delete from INT` left baselines/fail-baseline.tsv by edit; local.t's two unnamed `local $SIG{...}` rows ('foo' vs 'main::foo') pass too (sweep TOTAL 18686 -> 18690, commit "sweep baselines edited row by row").
OPEN: the `__WARN__` / `__DIE__` keys are plain hash slots, not signal slots, so `$SIG{__WARN__} = "h"` still reads back `h` (magic.t `Can assign to __WARN__` / `Can delete from __WARN__` stay blessed).  The fix is the same qualification at those two keys' store.
subject: %SIG is an ordinary hash in PCL, so a STRING handler name is returned verbatim; perl's magic hash qualifies it with the current package for a real signal name (4 op/magic.t rows)
